texts.preamble: Ibrahimbhai Kalabhai vs State Of Gujarat on 18 March, 2026 R/Cr.Ra/560/2009 Judgmen In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/Criminal Revision Application No. 560 of 2009 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar ============================================ Approved for Reporting Yes No ============================================ Ibrahimbhai Kalabhai Versus State Of Gujarat & Anr. ============================================ Appearance: Mr Mb Parikh(576) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 Public Prosecutor for the Respondent(s) No. 1 Rule Served for the Respondent(s) No. 2 = = = = == = = = = == Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar Date : 18/03/2026 Judgment
texts.facts: Hence, the present Revision Application is filed by the applicants-accused. Hence, requested to extend the benefit of amendment.
texts.arguments: 2) Learned Advocate for the applicant has submitted that both the Courts have committed error in convicting the applicant as the evidence is not properly appreciated more particularly failed to consider the evidence produced by the Food Inspector at Exhibit 29 and helper at Exhibit 62, both the evidence are self contrary evidence and they have committed error in taking the sample of ice candy (kulfi) and the evidence of collection of sample is not trustworthy. In the cross-examination also they have admitted that the stick was not removed from the ice candy and they had purchased four kulfies from the accused but there is a clear breach of Rule 22. The panch witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution and inspector also not clarified about obtaining training qua collecting the sample. Even the sample is not properly sent for analysis. 3) Learned APP for respondent - State has submitted that both the Courts have rightly convicted the applicant and as there is concurrent finding no interference of this Court is required and requested to dismiss the present application. Hence, once sample is found sub-standard without discussing further on merits and in view of provision of Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, and in light of the judgment in Nemi Chand v. State of Rajasthan, reported in (2018) 17 SCC 448, and Triloki Chand v. State of Himachal Pradesh, reported in (2020) 10 SCC 763, this Court is of the view that the applicant has already undergone 10 days sentence and paid Rs.1,000/- as fine and since concurrent finding is there, the sentence of six months simple imprisonment NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/560/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/03/2026 undefined is modified to 10 days imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/- (One Thousand) will serve the ends of justice.
